items.t: Dubai and Abu Dhabi among the world’s top 15 maritime cities
sum: The ‘Leading Maritime Cities 2026’ report ranks Dubai as the leading maritime city in the Middle East and Abu Dhabi, for the first time, among the world’s top 15
The ‘Leading Maritime Cities 2026’ study, compiled by DNV and Menon Economics, reveals that Dubai ranks as the leading maritime city in the Middle East and 12th globally.
Abu Dhabi has entered the top 15 for the first time, having risen to 15th place from 22nd in the previous edition.

This ranking highlights the growing importance of both Emirati cities on the international stage. Dubai achieved fifth place in the new ranking for maritime resilience, and was named the second most attractive city for relocating maritime headquarters.

This report, which is published every two years, ranks 50 maritime cities based on their scores across five categories: maritime transport; maritime finance and law; ports and logistics; and attractiveness and competitiveness.
The biennial report assesses 50 maritime cities across five categories: maritime transport, maritime finance and law, maritime technology, ports and logistics, and attractiveness and competitiveness.
For the assessments, DNV and Menon Economics draw on a panel of 208 high-level maritime experts from around the world.

Iberdrola stock rises as nine-month profit reaches EUR 5.82 billion
sum: Iberdrola reported a stronger first nine months of 2026 on October 22, with investment, grid assets and earnings all advancing, according to Atalayar. Reported net income reached 5.816 billion euros, up 10% from the year-earlier period. Adjusted net income rose 9% to 5.141 billion euros, or 13% excluding the effect of exchange rates.

Iberdrola stock traded at 23.56 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:55 CET on Friday, November 13, 2026, 0.26 percent above the Xetra close of Thursday, November 12. The quote keeps the share close to its recent trading range while investors weigh the companys investment-led growth plan against currency effects and financing costs.

The main operational driver was the networks business. Iberdrola invested 10.087 billion euros through September, 13% more than a year earlier. Networks absorbed 6.277 billion euros, or 62% of total investment, while the regulated asset base increased 14% to 56 billion euros. Transmission assets grew 31%.

The company said more than 90% of its network investment was directed to the United Kingdom, the United States and Brazil. Generation and customer activities received 3.6 billion euros, including 3.257 billion euros for renewable generation. Iberdrola installed 3,300 megawatts over the past 12 months and plans to add 15,000 megawatts between 2025 and 2030.

Adjusted EBITDA rose 7% to 11.891 billion euros in the nine-month period, with growth reaching 8% after removing exchange-rate effects. The company raised its 2026 outlook and now expects adjusted net income to increase by at least 10%. It also aims to maintain average annual adjusted-income growth of 10% over the next five years.

The strategy points to regulated networks as the central source of visibility. Iberdrola expects its regulated asset base to exceed 90 billion euros by 2030. The company plans to provide more detail at its Capital Markets Day in March 2027, giving investors a scheduled milestone for assessing the pace of capital deployment and earnings growth.
Shareholder distributions also increased. The interim dividend rose 8.7% to 0.275 euros per share, with a supplementary payment subject to approval at the 2027 Annual Shareholders Meeting.

Earthquake at Nvidia: Jensen Huang resigns amid an espionage scandal and stock market debacle
sum: The architect of the artificial intelligence boom steps down from the helm of the company after a double bombshell

The shock resignation has struck like a meteorite on Wall Street. Jensen Huang is no longer running Nvidia. The tycoon who brought chips into our daily lives has found himself forced to exit through the back door.

But what exactly happened? The dismissal is a chain of events combining ongoing investigations by the FBI and the US Congress into an alleged informant for the Beijing regime, alongside a scandal uncovered within the heart of the company itself involving one of its vice presidents.

Against this backdrop, the markets reacted with a dizzying U-turn that wiped out more than $600 billion in value in the space of four days. Shares plunged by over 10% before the market opened, hitting lows unseen in 14 years.

Faced with this situation, the Board of Directors convened an absolute emergency night-time summit aimed at stopping the bleeding at all costs. The result? Huang out and Colette Kress, the chief financial officer, placed at the helm on an interim basis whilst shareholders brace for foreseeable lawsuits from major company investors.

The eye of the storm has a name and surname: Alice Huang. This former Megaspeed executive—the commercial partner handling Nvidia's operations in Southeast Asia—is under the scrutiny of US authorities.
Investigators are looking into whether the company acted as a front to illegally divert billions in advanced semiconductors to China, brazenly bypassing Washington's vetoes.

Iberdrola stock edges higher as New York grid plan advances
sum: Iberdrola has launched a program through its US subsidiary Avangrid to renew and modernize 1,300 kilometers of electricity transmission lines in New York State. The company listed the initiative on November 8, 2026, as part of its wider push to strengthen networks as electricity demand rises.

Iberdrola stock traded at 22.97 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 12:20 CET on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, 0.09 percent above the Xetra close of Monday, November 9. The calculation uses the Xetra quote for Iberdrola under symbol IBE1.DE and compares the latest Lang & Schwarz price with the prior session close.

The work covers more than 230 transmission lines and is scheduled to run through 2031, according to Iberdrola’s corporate information. The initiative is designed to modernize existing infrastructure and prepare the network for future electricity demand in the state.

The project places regulated networks at the center of Iberdrola’s investment case. On its investor website, the company says electrical networks are the backbone of electrification and plans to invest 37 billion euros in networks through 2028. Avangrid gives the Spanish utility exposure to regulated transmission and distribution operations across the United States.

For investors, the announcement adds a long-dated infrastructure project to a strategy built around regulated assets, renewable generation and rising electrification demand. The program’s multi-year timetable may support visibility for network investment, while execution, regulation and financing remain important factors for the stock.

items.t: Iberdrola stock slips 1.18% from latest report as outlook holds
sum: Iberdrola raised its full-year 2026 adjusted-profit growth outlook to at least 10 percent on October 21 after reporting its nine-month results. The company said networks led operating growth, while its investment program continued to expand across key markets.

The Iberdrola release reported net profit of 5.8 billion euros for the first nine months, up 10 percent year on year. Adjusted net profit rose 9 percent to 5.1 billion euros, or 13 percent excluding foreign-exchange effects.

Adjusted EBITDA increased 7 percent to 11.9 billion euros, with the networks business providing the main operating support. Iberdrola said network investment reached 6.3 billion euros, up 28 percent, while the regulated asset base rose 14 percent to 56 billion euros.

The company targets average annual adjusted-profit growth of 10 percent over the next five years. It expects the global regulated asset base to exceed 90 billion euros by 2030 and plans to add 15 gigawatts of power-generation capacity between 2025 and 2030. Further strategic details are scheduled for the Capital Markets Day in March 2027.

Iberdrola stock traded at 22.61 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 17:45 CET on Friday, November 6, 2026, 1.82 percent below the Xetra close of Thursday, November 5. The move is separate from the 1.18 percent decline from the 22.88 euros cited in the previous report on November 5.

Why Grupo Financiero Galicia Bears Were Right Before The Drop
sum: Holding Grupo Financiero Galicia over the past year would have meant a 39.1% loss, including dividends. If you had committed capital on 4 November 2025, that outcome would probably feel jarring next to analyst models that pointed to rising earnings, mid‑teens profit margins and higher P/E multiples. With revenue dipping yet net income and net margin rising in Q2 2026, what exactly did the original investment case fail to allow for in those specific assumptions?
Grupo Financiero Galicia has already moved. See which of 194 high quality undervalued stocks still trade below our estimates.
The Two Stories Investors Had To Weigh On Grupo Financiero Galicia
The shares cost ARS9,065 at the start of the period, so anyone looking at Grupo Financiero Galicia then was really choosing between two very different futures.

The optimistic version was based on the integration of Galicia Más and a growing digital banking ecosystem, with a Fair Value of ARS11,189, a price implied by assumptions of 30.5% revenue growth and a 19.5% profit margin over three years.

The cautious view focused on deteriorating credit quality and fintech pressure, with a Fair Value of ARS5,591 and an assumption that revenue would grow 24.5% with profit margin also settling at 19.5%.

The clearest new fact was Q2 2026 performance. Grupo Financiero Galicia reported total revenue of ARS1,869,395.532m versus ARS1,929,753.668m a year earlier, while net income excluding extra items rose to ARS258,321.872m from ARS230,554.011m and net margin moved from 11.4% to 13.8%. That pattern of softer top line but higher profitability had implications for both more optimistic and more cautious interpretations.

Iberdrola stock gets 2026 profit outlook boost from power networks
sum: Iberdrola raised its 2026 adjusted-profit outlook on Wednesday, October 21, after reporting stronger results for the first nine months. The Spanish utility now expects adjusted net profit to grow by at least 10% this year, compared with previous guidance for growth above 8%, according to Reuters.

Reported net profit for the nine months rose 10 percent to 5.8 billion euros. Adjusted net profit increased 9 percent to 5.1 billion euros, while the company said the adjusted increase would have been 13 percent excluding foreign-exchange effects.

Adjusted EBITDA advanced 7 percent to 11.9 billion euros. The networks business was the main contributor, with EBITDA up 15 percent as Iberdrola expanded its regulated asset base and benefited from a higher contribution from transmission assets.

The performance supports Iberdrola's shift toward regulated infrastructure. The company expects the global regulated asset base to exceed 90 billion euros by 2030, compared with 56 billion euros currently, and plans to add 15 gigawatts of power capacity by the end of the decade. The strategy combines grid investment with a more selective approach to renewable-generation projects.

Iberdrola invested 10.1 billion euros in the first nine months, with networks accounting for the largest share. The company's investor-relations page lists 5.81 billion euros of reported net profit, 11.89 billion euros of adjusted EBITDA and 64,881 gigawatt-hours of renewable generation for the period. The figures are available on the Iberdrola investor page.

Iberdrola also proposed an interim shareholder payout of 0.275 euros per share, an increase of 8.7 percent, with a supplementary dividend to be announced in 2027 after the shareholders' meeting. Management is targeting average annual adjusted-profit growth of 10 percent over the next five years.

The real-time quote of Iberdrola stock traded at 22.19 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:01 CET on Monday, November 2, 2026, 0.05 percent below the Xetra close of Friday, October 30. The movement kept the share near its most recent Xetra reference while investors assessed the higher earnings outlook and the capital requirements of Iberdrola's network expansion.

Mainova (DB:MNV6) Stock Could Be 18% Overvalued On Its Dividend Case
sum: Mainova has delivered a solid positive return over the past year, yet its longer track record is weaker, which puts the focus squarely on whether the current share price is still aligned with the dividend stream investors receive. For anyone following Mainova stock today, the central puzzle is how that dividend profile stacks up against what the market is willing to pay.
- Over the past 5 years the share price declined 23.8%, which puts real weight on the question of whether the dividend stream alone can justify where the stock trades now.

- The business relies heavily on converting regulated and infrastructure driven cash flows into reliable distributions, so the stability and timing of those payouts can matter as much as headline earnings when thinking about valuation.
- What if you looked at Mainova through its earnings instead? See why Mainova's 11.8x P/E tells a different valuation story.
The issue now is whether Mainova's current market price is justified by the dividend stream that the Dividend Discount Model (DDM) points to over the long run.
If you want to stress test this same dividend question beyond Mainova, you can scan a wider field of income ideas using 221 dividend fortresses.

The Dividend Discount Model (DDM) values Mainova by projecting its future dividend stream and discounting it back to today. For this stock, the model leans heavily on the balance between current payout and a relatively restrained growth outlook. The inputs use a dividend per share of €10.84, a return on equity of 7.71% and a payout ratio of about 40.10%. Together, these point to a modest dividend growth rate of 2.05% that is capped from a higher initial figure.
